name: Warren Buffett
why: The ultimate baseline for blue-chip compounding, cash generation, and financial giants.

name: David Tepper
why: Highly agile trader known for massive macroeconomic pivots and aggressive tech/semiconductor bets.

name: Bill Ackman
why: Typically holds fewer than 10 large-cap names; excellent for analyzing deep corporate operational plays.

name: Bill Ackman (Pershing Square Inc.)
why: Pershing Square Inc. now files the 13F-HR holdings; the LP entity files 13F-NT notices. Track both for completeness.

name: Seth Klarman
why: The "Oracle of Boston" looks for complex, unloved, or mispriced assets with strict downside protection.

name: Stanley Druckenmiller
why: Renowned for an unblemished multi-decade track record, blending macro trends with high-conviction equity themes.

name: Howard Marks
why: Master of market cycles; tracking his equity moves reveals where he sees deep value amidst market credit stress.

name: Chase Coleman
why: The premier "Tiger Cub" tracking early-to-late stage software, internet, and disruptive global consumer tech.

name: Daniel Loeb
why: Looks for catalysts like spin-offs, corporate restructurings, or management shakeups to unlock value.

name: Paul Singer
why: A powerhouse activist that forces corporate governance overhauls; tracking hints at impending corporate shakeups.

name: Li Lu
why: Heavily influenced by Charlie Munger; runs a highly concentrated book focused on pristine, long-term compounders.

name: Ray Dalio
why: The world's largest hedge fund; his All Weather approach reveals diversified macro positioning across asset classes.

name: Carl Icahn
why: The original activist investor; notorious for proxy fights and forcing spin-offs, dividends, and board changes.

name: George Soros
why: Quantum Fund legend who broke the Bank of England; tracks macro trends with bold, asymmetric conviction bets.

name: Cathie Wood
why: The face of innovation investing; high-conviction bets on AI, genomics, robotics, blockchain, and energy storage.

name: Israel Englander
why: One of the most prolific 13F filers by volume; massive diversified book reveals cross-sector institutional flows.

name: Ken Griffin
why: Citadel's massive book spans equities, derivatives, and fixed income; a barometer for institutional positioning.

name: Jim Simons
why: The legendary mathematician-turned-quant; Renaissance's Medallion Fund is the gold standard of systematic trading.

name: Cliff Asness
why: Pioneer of factor-based investing; AQR's book reveals institutional tilts toward value, momentum, and alternative betas.
